assumptions: No traction, customer commitments, specialist agreements, or economics exist beyond what is explicitly stated in the packet.
The service can be structured lawfully with qualified customs professionals owning regulated advice and representation, but their availability, cost, insurance, and liability terms remain uncertain.

At least one EU importer vertical may have recurring difficult-classification work, but the scoring does not assume that its case density, account density, or willingness to pay has been demonstrated.
Permission to reuse confidential or de-identified case outcomes is not assumed; the proposed data advantage is therefore treated as conditional rather than present.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Name one vertical and show a paid annual pilot with repeated difficult-SKU cases, quantified customer loss avoided, renewal intent, and a demonstrable advantage over incumbent managed services; also show actual expert hours and cost, gross margin, direct-sales CAC and payback, enforceable professional-liability terms, and either explicit reusable-data rights or a defensibility mechanism that does not depend on them.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The candidate correctly recognizes that free official filing, public rulings, and automated code lookup push paid value toward difficult product-fact development, expert-reviewed reasoning, monitoring, and exception handling. That is a coherent wedge, but it is an adaptation to an established category rather than a demonstrated proprietary insight, and incumbents already cover much of it.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Misclassification can affect duties, licences, restrictions, and the validity of binding decisions, so difficult cases can carry meaningful risk. However, no named vertical, loss frequency, case volume, paid pilot, price acceptance, or renewal evidence is present, while official WIT filing is free and basic research is accessible.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Annual monitoring plus separately priced expert cases could combine recurring revenue with automation leverage, and the stated capital requirement fits the founder's available capital. Yet pricing, expert utilization, gross margin, CAC, payback, retention, support load, insurance, cash generation, and the founder-wealth path are all unknown; qualified review and escalation may keep the model service-heavy.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: A single repeat-SKU vertical is appropriately narrow in concept and the EU provides geographic room, but the beachhead has not actually been selected or sized. There is no evidence that a reachable segment combines enough difficult cases, insufficient internal capability, and enough accounts to support a meaningful business.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Direct importer ownership removes dependence on a conflicted forwarder channel and vertical specialization could support a niche position. Still, Avalara, eClear, TariffPilot, and large logistics providers already offer overlapping automation, reasoning, expertise, APIs, and consulting, and the candidate has no proven exclusive channel, integration, data right, or performance edge.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: If one vertical workflow succeeds, adjacent product categories, rule monitoring, disputes, appeals, and other EU markets are plausible extensions. Expansion is only moderately attractive because vertical knowledge may transfer imperfectly, professional delivery must scale with it, and incumbents already serve broad catalogues and geographies.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Embedded product history, fact templates, direct renewal relationships, and permissioned outcomes could accumulate into switching costs and lower expert effort. Those assets are presently conditional on customer data rights and sufficient case flow; public rulings, accessible official sources, a slow 120-day outcome cycle, and copyable workflow software substantially weaken the proposed moat.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A confidential, vertical-specific intake and exception workflow may be more relevant than a generic code recommender, but the packet provides no evidence that it is materially faster, safer, cheaper, more accurate, or more trusted than incumbent managed classification. Expert review, reasoned outputs, bulk workflows, and APIs are already marketed by competitors.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Persistent EU customs complexity and modern AI make structured evidence workflows cheaper to build and operate. The same AI trend also accelerates commoditization, and the packet identifies no new regulatory deadline, distribution opening, or other catalyst that gives this entrant a privileged window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Direct account-based outreach avoids making forwarders an indispensable channel and can be tested with limited initial spend. It is nevertheless entirely unvalidated, likely trust-intensive and slow, has unknown reachable account density and CAC, and may conflict with the founder's part-time availability and preference to minimize sustained social selling.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and automation skills fit the product layer, AI can accelerate implementation, and the proposed capital is within the stated limit. Execution still depends on qualified specialists, accurate product facts, professional insurance and liability allocation, lawful representation, enterprise sales, and expert escalation while the founder remains employed; these constraints are not replaceable by AI.

highest_value_structural_change: Make the product an embedded product-information and classification control layer at the mandatory new-SKU release gate for one chosen vertical, with structured fact completion on every SKU and qualified experts reviewing only flagged exceptions. That would create recurring workflow ownership, case density, switching costs, and scalable delivery without making optional reuse of confidential outcomes the sole compounding asset.
main_structural_strength: The design focuses on the non-commodity portion of classification work and owns the direct importer renewal relationship, allowing a vertical workflow and expert exception layer to become valuable if repeat case density is established.
primary_score_limiter: The opportunity has no identified, sized, or paid beachhead proving that recurring difficult-classification pain is dense enough to support annual contracts, scalable expert economics, and repeatable direct acquisition.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Mature providers already market automated classification, official-source reasoning, bulk processing, APIs, and human-expert review, while official Polish WIT filing is free and core rulings and tariff research are public; the proposed paid workflow therefore lacks a demonstrated behavior-changing advantage.
